summary: All three tokens occur within the explicitly identified Classical Syriac hymn and episcopal response in 66/279. They provide cognate/contact material, not Turoyo inflectional evidence.

Pšuṭ yaminox is a command to extend the right hand; dafšaṭ iḏe refers to Jesus extending his hand; nefšuṭ yamine belongs to the prayer that he extend his right hand. The source itself identifies these passages as lešono oromoyo.
No Turoyo Imperativ, Infectum or stem III is added from these tokens. The existing I forms and boxes are retained unchanged, and no new sense or idiom is proposed.
The comparative Afel interpretation of dafšaṭ and the stem of nefšuṭ remain uncertain in this oral rendering. These questions do not warrant a new native paradigm.
The grammatical comparison and religious setting are recorded here rather than inserted into glossary form labels.
In the oral Classical Syriac hymn, confirm the stem and vocalization of dafšaṭ and nefšuṭ. This is a comparison question, not evidence for new Turoyo stems.
